contracts.scope: Ballot-only provider. Full-log deployments select LogStore instead; no duplicate log stack.
Synchronous bounded worker interface; no async runtime yet.
Version-1 vote framing. Different physical formats require migration.
Static bootstrap, atomic entries/hard-state/commit, suffix fencing and durably pinned snapshot bases. Physical WAL reclamation remains pending.
Same platform contract as VoteIo, with separate selected native storage binding.
Bounded version-2 entry/bootstrap/transition framing.
Deterministic bounded counter and exact operation retries; checkpoint capability is an explicit extension.
Immutable read after exact one-use quorum barrier and applied-prefix check. Host query/result types are supported; no clock leases.
One local group per logical handle, bounded stage/seal and atomic publication. Shared drivers compose peer installation with authoritative log persistence and application restore.
Durable local log anchors and atomic two-slot pin switches. Logical compaction and verified recovery; physical WAL cleaning and general backup retention remain pending.
Exclusive two-slot I/O; data and file-name sync precede root publication.
Version-1 CRC32C framing with bounded bootstrap/application data. No cryptographic provenance claim.
Complete value/boundary/dedup state with exact capacity/schema validation. Host schema and state are composable.
Unique bounded readiness with fair requeue; Shard owns cores and enforces item/byte/time visits, ingress credits and scoped single-owner access. Caller-driven, no hidden threads.
Bounded ordered deadlines with exact scoped tokens, replacement/cancellation and lateness. TimedShard supplies automatic consensus timer management through this public seam.

Single-owner automatic election/heartbeat deadlines, exact queued expiration fencing, bounded overload retry and explicit provider failure. Caller supplies monotonic time and bounded effect workers. No deadline-derived read authority.
Local monotonic milliseconds with clone-shared epoch; virtual host clock injection. No core clock reads or diagnostic wall-clock API.

Explicit owned batches, separate written/durable stages, one pending transition per group, bounded request/unit/capacity-byte retention with control reserves and terminal-delivery credit release. The selected store remains authoritative; cores stay on their owner. Native close drains accepted work and try_reclaim returns the store. Three-node/100-group integration covers replication, read barriers, retries, leader replacement and actual-file restart.
Injected nonblocking completion hint, never durable evidence. Shared host resources remain host-owned.

Version-1 same-peer owned batches, node/peer request/message/capacity-byte ceilings, control reserves, snapshot ceilings, fair peer/class visits and credit retention through local completion. Local completion is not a Raft acknowledgement. No wire format, sockets, security or persistent delivery claim; transport remains pending.

Independent wire format 1 for all current static-configuration RPCs, same-peer multiplexing, fixed validated prefix, bounded lengths/counts/decoded retention and trusted peer-scope consistency. Native worker and recursive snapshot histories traverse frames. A host-only single-fixture provider tests the public seam, not full alternative codec conformance. No socket/authentication or wire snapshot chunk protocol.
Explicitly seeded reproducible election jitter; independent node seeds supplied by host. No cryptographic/identity use.
